note_en: Repeating 谁…谁… in one clause isn't two questions but a general rule: "whoever …, that person …." 饭谁有空谁做 "whoever is free does the cooking"; 谁有时间谁做 "whoever has time does it." With a negative the meaning shifts: 谁也不觉得应该谁多做一点 "neither of them felt that either one should do more" — the first 谁 means "no one," the second "someone." English translates each 谁 differently, though Chinese uses the same word.
